title: Knowledge node (aggregate or diagnostic)
description: One entry of knowledge-eval/data/nodes_<subject>_6up.json. This schema is applied to the raw objects in that file: nothing renames fields or reshapes arrays before validation (see scripts/check_schema.py). An aggregate node is a chapter and carries no questions; only a diagnostic node can be judged weak.

node_id.description: Stable business key. Diagnostic nodes end in -dNN, chapter aggregates in -uNN, the end-of-term review in -u-review.

parent_id.description: For a diagnostic node, the chapter's -uNN code. Null on aggregates.

chapter_order.description: Where the chapter sits in the book. The picker orders 'current / already taught / not yet taught' by this number, so it must come from the node itself rather than from a unit row a question points at.

week_start.description: Aggregate only: the school week this chapter is normally taught in. Drives calendar auto-advance.

knowledge_type.description: Optional, and required only in practice on diagnostic nodes. It is deliberately absent on aggregates: inventing one per subject to satisfy a non-null column is what the previous revision did wrong.

micro_nodes.description: The textbook's own sub-points, as plain strings. At least one: a node nobody can name a sub-point for is not diagnosable.

ability_lines.description: Diagnostic nodes only, and required there in practice. Which ability lines this node can actually be asked about — the drill-down judges each one on its own window, so a line listed here costs three questions. Two lines minimum: a node with one line has nothing to drill into, and check_content has always required two tags per node. Do not list a line to look complete: 数学的「用有序数对确定位置」没有可执行的计算，语文的「文言朗读停顿」没有习作任务，硬凑出来的格子只会产出废题。Aggregates carry none: a chapter has no questions.

source_ids.description: Optional. The taxonomy ids behind micro_nodes, in the same order. Present for maths (the vendored snapshot has 38); absent for 语文/英语, whose sub-points have no public taxonomy.

prerequisite_node_ids.description: Node ids that should be solid first. A taxonomy id (mt_g6u_...) is accepted where the source material states the prerequisite at micro-point level instead of node level.
